question: I maintain a GitHub-hosted application and want Docker Hub to build and publish its image when I push to the main branch, but only after container tests pass. How should I set this up, verify the builds, and handle common failures, including a possible private submodule?

I maintain a Dockerfile that uses a base image and downloads a remote file. How should I set up a build policy so our builds accept images from approved registries and permit only HTTPS downloads, then check that the policy behaves as intended before using it in our builds?

I maintain a growing codebase and want a Docker Agent coding assistant in my ACP-capable editor to find relevant code by meaning without loading the whole repository into its prompt. How should I configure the searchable source and editor integration, then check that it works and choose sensible operating options?

Our organization has a DHI Select subscription and needs a FIPS variant of a Python image with an additional company certificate for a regulated service. As the platform engineer, how should I find and mirror the right repository, create the customized image, and check that the resulting image is suitable to hand to the application team?

I manage two application containers on one Linux Docker host. They need to reach each other by name, while a web endpoint should initially be reachable only from the host. How should I set up and check their networking, and what changes if we later need access from another host or have a legacy application that requires a physical-network identity?

A community issue asks for a new Docker documentation guide with platform-specific steps and links to existing product pages. As a contributor, how should I prepare a focused, reviewable pull request?

I'm an IT administrator rolling out Docker Desktop to managed Windows devices through Intune. How should I prepare the deployment so the installation and organization settings are consistent, users can sign in under our policy, and I can verify when a restart or update is needed?

Our team already runs PostgreSQL in Docker Compose with persistent development data. How can I add a browser-based database interface that teammates can start without repeated login prompts, connect it to the database without publishing the database port, and check that it is ready? Include ways to preserve the interface's settings, diagnose connection-address mistakes, and assess what must change before using shared or sensitive data.

I'm replacing a shell-based Docker smoke test with a Go application that runs Alpine's `echo hello world` command and waits for completion. How should I implement it and prepare the SDK connection, including on Docker Desktop for Linux, when the Docker client and daemon may have different versions?

I'm the owner of a Docker organization onboarding 1,200 colleagues from an email export. How should I prepare capacity, invite them with appropriate roles, and restrict Docker Desktop use to organization members? Include checks that prevent onboarding blockers and options for managing future joiners through our identity provider.

I maintain a containerized development app in Docker Desktop. A teammate's CI-built image produces errors and slowdowns with our existing data. How can I copy the app's volume, run a separate test instance against that copy, and use Desktop's container logs and build inspection tools to investigate? I need to preserve the original data and account for any interruption to containers using it.

I own a Docker organization and maintain a Node.js service whose image contains Express 4.17.1. We have different versions running in staging and production. How can I enable ongoing Scout analysis, investigate application and base-image vulnerabilities, publish a corrected candidate, and compare it with production before deciding to promote it? Include build-attestation constraints and how to keep tracking security improvements after the initial fix.

I'm preparing a Spring Boot application's S3 and SQS integration-test environment for parallel CI builds. How should I configure the project and test harness to avoid real AWS calls and conflicting ports, verify that the environment runs and cleans up, and evaluate a cloud runtime if container workloads strain our development machines?

I’m a .NET developer with the add-db sample and its local database development setup already configured. Before handing it off for a deployment rehearsal, how should I check database persistence, run containerized unit tests locally and during image builds, and prepare the Docker Desktop Kubernetes manifest? Include the image and repository prerequisites for using an image published through GitHub Actions, and keep the configuration aligned with the documented sample.

I maintain a working React/MUI Docker extension prototype and want to prepare it for Marketplace submission. What UI changes and local verification should I prioritize so it fits Docker Desktop, remains maintainable as its appearance changes, and is ready for the documented submission process? Include how to package the release information and handle subsequent updates.
